boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Sabine Pass II record (September 8, 1863) in Operations to Blockade the Texas Coast [September 1863]. The expedition's embarkation from New Orleans on September 4, its return by September 11 and Banks's later Rio Grande expedition are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives 4 gunboats and 7 transports with troops and the Davis Guards as 44 men (CS bounds 44 and 44); the live field reads CS 44 and NPS 44 men. Dowling says he captured the gunboats with 47 men and that twenty-two vessels had gathered. Franklin says about 700 infantry, a field battery and eight heavy guns were inside the bar by 10 o'clock with 700 more aground on it, and 1,200 infantry that could be landed after the engagement; Weitzel's advance had about 1,000 infantry.
claims.rationale: Garrison and embarked-force figures of different moments and scopes: Weitzel's 1,000 at embarkation on September 4; 700 inside the bar and 700 aground at about 10 a.m. on September 8; 1,200 landable after the engagement; Dowling's 47 in the fort on September 8. Magruder's 40 and 15,000 (read, not selected) are not used. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.rationale: Stated plans from interested reports; NPS's statement of intent to begin occupying Texas is a summary.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Lieutenant Richard W. Dowling, Major General William B. Franklin and Captain Frederick Crocker (navy); the live page gives Franklin as brigadier general, not adopted. Dowling commanded the fort. Franklin says the plan was adopted with Crocker and that he decided to recross the bar. Crocker says the Granite City and General Banks made no attempt to follow and blames Franklin for failing to co-operate; Franklin says Weitzel's report shows why the landing could not be carried out.
claims.rationale: Opposing interested accounts of responsibility; neither is adopted, and no automatic sole credit.

claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads US 230 and CS unknown; the live field reads 350 (US 350; CS 0); NPS says about 200 prisoners. Dowling says about 350 prisoners were taken with two gunboats and thirteen guns. Franklin says there were no losses beyond those Weitzel reported (not selected). No Confederate loss figure appears in the selected reports.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Prisoner counts include naval crews; the frozen 230 is not traced.

open_questions: Magruder's and Odlum's reports (read, not selected), Weitzel's report and loss figures (read, not selected), the naval reports cited by the compiler (Annual Report of the Secretary of the Navy, 1863), returns and charts remain deferred. Crocker's report is the targeted follow-up for the command dispute.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Franklin's September 11 and 14, 1863 reports and Dowling's September 9, 1863 report are interested accounts from opposite sides; Crocker's September 12 report, written as a prisoner, is a separate family used as the follow-up. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
